title: The Wrong Harvest
premise: Folklorist Wendell Coldharbour returns to the village of Harrow's Bend to record its harvest songs, only to find his childhood imaginary friend, Tam, waiting on his porch—unchanged after thirty years. The village's founding families long ago invited something into their fields in exchange for abundance, and each generation must renew the invitation with a song sung twice; Wendell's recordings have been breaking that cycle by capturing what was never meant to be repeated. As the night of the wrong harvest unfolds, he learns he is himself an inheritance—the unclaimed portion owed to the field—and must choose between burning the songs and letting the village pay its debt, ending with him singing the song a second time alone, binding the thing to himself and freeing Harrow's Bend at the cost of never being believed again.
about_author: Gideon Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from farming communities across the English countryside. Their fiction draws on half-remembered field recordings and the unsettling habit villages have of agreeing on stories they claim not to believe.

chapters.title: The Song Nobody Sings Twice
chapters.summary: Wendell arrives in Harrow's Bend with recording equipment and fifteen years of rationalizations. In the pub, an old woman begins the harvest song, stops mid-verse, and leaves without paying for her drink. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: unease dressed as professional curiosity—the first crack in his armor of explanations.

chapters.title: Tam on the Porch
chapters.summary: At his late mother's cottage, Wendell finds Tam—his childhood imaginary friend—sitting on the porch steps, exactly as he left him at age nine. Tam speaks only in fragments of the old song. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: terror braided with a shameful, aching relief at being recognized by something.

chapters.title: What the Registers Omit
chapters.summary: Digging through parish records, Wendell finds every founding family listed except one name scratched out across two centuries—and his own surname added in fresh ink. The vicar warns him off gently, then not so gently. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the horror of discovering you are already written into something.

chapters.title: The Field That Answers
chapters.summary: Wendell records the empty farmland at dusk; playback reveals a second voice beneath his own, singing verses no villager will repeat. Tam stands at the field's edge, mouthing along. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: vertigo as his instruments confirm what his childhood always knew.

chapters.title: Debts of the Founding Families
chapters.summary: The innkeeper's daughter, Maren, breaks silence: the invitation renews each generation, and this year the singers refuse because the last renewal took her brother. She shows Wendell the tally of names owed. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into defiance, and the first alliance.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Trapped overnight by a storm, Wendell confronts his own history: the noises, the disappearances, the mother who never let him sing indoors. Tam grows more solid as Wendell's denial thins. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the collapse of rationalization—belonging revealed as a trap he was born into.

chapters.title: The Invitation Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Maren and Wendell find the original covenant hidden in the church floor: the field was promised 'one of the blood, unclaimed.' Wendell realizes the scratched-out name is his line—he was inherited like property. POV: alternating Wendell and Maren. Emotional beat: cold fury; justice outside any law begins here.

chapters.title: Night of the Wrong Harvest
chapters.summary: The village attempts a substitute offering; the field rejects it, and the thing in the rows walks toward the cottages while Tam holds the boundary, screaming in Wendell's childhood voice. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: communal panic, courage failing, the cost of broken bargains made visible.

chapters.title: One Voice, Sung Twice
chapters.summary: At the field's heart, Wendell understands: a song captured can be broken, but a song given freely binds. He sings the harvest song twice, alone, offering himself as the unclaimed blood. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: terrible agency—choosing inheritance instead of fleeing it.

chapters.title: After the Reaping
chapters.summary: Dawn. The field lies fallow and silent; Tam is gone, or finally real enough to rest. Maren burns the recordings with Wendell's blessing. He stays in Harrow's Bend—not forgiven, but belonging at last. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace shadowed by everything the village will never admit happened.
